# AI runtime and provider plan

**Canonical for:** provider taxonomy, runtime kinds, transport routing and the MCP boundary.

## Five concepts, never conflated

- **capability** — WHAT the system can do. Owned by a LEGO. Stable. Example: `agent.session`.
- **implementation** — HOW a capability is realised. Swappable. Example: a JS implementation or a Rust implementation.
- **provider** — WHERE an implementation is sourced from. Example kinds: model-provider, tool-provider, application-provider.
- **transport** — HOW bytes move. Example: in-process, worker, http, mcp.
- **runtime** — WHERE an agent or system executes. Example kinds: agent-runtime, simulation-runtime.

```
capability -> contract -> operations -> interaction -> implementation -> provider -> transport -> runtime
```

**Anti-pattern:** Declaring `composio.github.repo.read` as a capability. That fuses capability (repo read), provider (Composio) and application (GitHub) into one identifier that cannot be replaced without a rename.

## Provider kinds

| Kind | Contract | Supplies | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `model-provider` | `ai.model-gateway` | Supplies inference. Text, embeddings, possibly tool-calling. | a hosted model gateway such as 9Router, a direct vendor API, a local model server |
| `tool-provider` | `ai.tool-gateway` | Supplies callable tools and readable resources to an agent. | a tool/app gateway such as Composio, a local tool pack, an MCP server |
| `application-provider` | `ai.application-provider` | An external application exposed as capabilities. Independent of whichever gateway reaches it. | GitHub, an issue tracker, a chat platform |
| `agent-runtime` | `ai.agent-runtime` | Executes an agent session. Owns the agent loop, not the model. | Hermes, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, OpenClaw, a DeepSeek harness |
| `simulation-runtime` | `ai.agent-runtime` | Executes a scenario or simulation rather than a task-directed agent. | MiroFish |

> A vendor name may appear in this file ONLY inside an `examples` array, and only as an illustration of a provider kind. No vendor may appear in an id, a required field, a code path or a default. If a vendor name is ever needed to make a contract work, the contract is wrong.

### Named examples and their planes

| Example | Plane | Kind | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 9Router | Model plane | model gateway | not implemented |
| Composio | Tool plane | tool/app gateway | not implemented |
| GitHub | Code plane | **native** application provider | not implemented |
| Hermes / Claude Code / Gemini CLI / OpenClaw / Antigravity | Agent plane | external agent runtime | not implemented |
| MiroFish | Simulation plane | simulation runtime | not implemented |

Two rules that follow: **GitHub is never forced through Composio** — a native
application provider and a gateway-reached one are two bindings of one
capability set. And **MCP never becomes the internal business architecture**.

## Transport routing

| When | Transport | Mechanism |
| --- | --- | --- |
| same process | `in-process` | direct dispatcher |
| local event | `in-process` | event dispatcher |
| process boundary | `worker` | IPC / worker adapter |
| remote service | `remote` | HTTP or a provider-defined protocol |
| external interoperability | `mcp` | MCP adapter |

Never force every call through HTTP. An HTTP hop between two objects in one process is the most expensive available way to call a function.

A transport advertises which interaction classes it can carry. The OPERATION owns its interaction class; a transport that cannot carry it is simply not eligible. A transport must never silently downgrade a STREAM to a CALL — the caller asked for incremental output and would instead wait for a single late response.

## MCP boundary

```
external world <-> MCP adapter <-> LEGO capability contract <-> implementation
```

- MCP is an interoperability ADAPTER at the edge. It must never become the internal application architecture.
- No internal LEGO may call another LEGO over MCP. Internal communication stays CALL/EVENT/STREAM/BATCH over the local dispatcher, as ADR-0004 requires.
- MCP concepts map ONTO the tool gateway contract; the tool gateway is not defined in MCP terms. If MCP changes, one adapter changes.
- Capabilities are exported explicitly and individually. There is no export-everything switch, because the set of capabilities safe to hand to an external client is never the full set.

**No MCP server, client, adapter or dependency exists in this repository.**

## Runtime adapter lifecycle

```
connect -> start -> send -> stream -> pause -> resume -> cancel -> status -> artifacts -> disconnect
```

External runtimes are NEVER reimplemented — in Rust or otherwise. They are adapted. Reimplementing a third-party agent harness means owning its bugs and its release cycle for no architectural gain.

## Resource profiles

| Profile | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `low-resource` | Runs on a phone, a Termux session or a 1GB VPS. No GPU, no persistent daemon, minimal memory. |
| `standard` | A normal laptop or small server. |
| `high-resource` | Needs substantial CPU or memory; not assumable on a user device. |
| `remote` | Executes elsewhere. Local cost is a network call; availability becomes a real failure mode. |

Runtime registry tracks: `cpu`, `memory`, `disk`, `network`, `latency`, `locality`, `startupCost`, `estimatedCost`, `availability`.

No external runtime may become a local installation requirement. Every AI provider is optional and remotely satisfiable, because requiring a local agent runtime would exclude the low-end targets the foundation explicitly supports.

## Zero-install

```
aiFoundation     ready
modelProvider    not-configured
toolProvider     not-configured
agentRuntime     not-configured
```

Reported as: capability-unavailable with reason 'no inference provider configured'

> The system must never fake inference, never return a canned completion and never pretend a provider exists. It reports that the foundation is ready and no provider is connected. A fake answer is worse than no answer, because the user cannot tell it is fake.
